title.narrative: Co-creation of a national technology-enabled program for weight management in Thailand

description.narrative: In an effort to tackle the growing burden of cardiovascular disease, Thailandâ€™s policy makers are planning to offer behavioural support to overweight individuals. Our evaluation of their planned intervention suggested low levels of engagement among end-users due to inadequate intensity and quality of support. Digital technology could be used to address these limitations economically but requires careful consideration of the context to ensure equitable participation of digitally underserved groups such as the elderly, rural/remote, and low-income populations.
Overweight (defined by Asian cut-off of body mass index greater than 23 kg/m2) adults over the age of 35 years.

We will work with Thailandâ€™s policy makers and healthcare providers to develop their proposed weight management intervention into state-of-the-art technology-enabled interventions that can deliver clinically important weight loss economically and reduce cardiovascular risk for diverse populations in Thailand. The specific objectives are to: - Undertake context (behavioural, technological, and organisational) analysis to inform intervention development - Co-create technology-enabled interventions for two price points being considered by the Thai policy makers, and assess their acceptability to diverse socio-demographic groups - Evaluate the effectiveness of intervention using a cluster randomised trial - Conduct economic evaluation and develop service standards for the interventions
